overview: Ward QI project on 7A and 7B using the Model for Improvement: a baseline year from existing weekly inspection data, then three PDSA cycles from November 2026 to April 2027 testing a protected night repositioning round, first without and then with a float nurse on poorly staffed nights, and finally with touch-based skin assessment.
population: All adult inpatients on wards 7A and 7B; the round covers patients scored at high risk at the evening handover.
exposure: Protected night repositioning round at 23:00, 02:00 and 05:00 by a named nurse, joined by a float nurse when the ratio is worse than one to seven and one is available; risk reassessed at the evening handover; touch-based assessment added in cycle 3.
procedures: Cycle 1 (November and December): round on 7A only, no float nurse. Cycle 2 (January and February): both wards, float nurse requested on qualifying nights. Cycle 3 (March and April): touch-based assessment added. Weekly skin inspection by tissue viability continues unchanged as the measurement source; the night nurse in charge records round completion and float availability on a ward sheet each night. Fortnightly huddle reviews the charts.

outcomes.name: Patient-days between category 2 or worse injuries
outcomes.measure: Patient-days between successive injuries found at weekly skin inspection, both wards combined, with a fixed counting rule
outcomes.timing: Continuously from the baseline year to April 2027
outcomes.why: Suited to rare events and not distorted by reporting behaviour.

outcomes.name: Monthly injury rate by night staffing
outcomes.measure: Category 2 or worse injuries per 1,000 patient-days, split by nights worse or better than one nurse to seven
outcomes.why: Shows whether the round protects patients on poorly staffed nights.

outcomes.name: Round completion
outcomes.measure: Proportion of scheduled round times completed, and float nurse availability on qualifying nights
outcomes.why: Separates a failed idea from failed delivery.

outcomes.name: Missed night medication doses
outcomes.measure: Proportion of scheduled night doses given more than one hour late, from the electronic administration record
outcomes.why: The round must not take time from other night care.

outcomes.name: Patients woken by the round
outcomes.measure: Yes or no question at the morning round for a sample of 10 patients per ward per week

feasibility: Uses existing staff, the night bank when available, and the existing weekly inspection; about 15 minutes per night for recording.
biasMitigation: Outcome from weekly inspection, not incident reports
Counting rule and chart rules fixed before cycle 1
Stratification by night staffing recorded from the roster, not by recollection
Co-interventions such as mattress changes annotated on the chart

biasFlags.label: Secular change in mattresses or policy
biasFlags.note: Annotate the chart; compare with other medical wards' incident trends.

biasFlags.label: Inspection drift
biasFlags.note: Tissue viability nurses may look harder during the project; double inspection of a 10 percent sample.

biasFlags.label: Blame of night nurses
biasFlags.note: Ward-level reporting only, as the constraints require.

flags: One process and two balancing measures; no causal claim about staffing
parsimony.simplestPath: One interval chart from existing inspections, three short cycles, one nightly completion sheet.

theoreticalFramework: Model for Improvement with PDSA cycles; SEIPS only to name work-system factors (staffing, tasks, tools) when revising the round.
summary: Three PDSA cycles with an interval measure from weekly inspection, a staffing-stratified secondary rate, one process and two balancing measures.
